position in the Internal Revenue Service without reference to the period
of his separation from the service.

October 11, 1893, to July 10, 1898, when hie was removed for political
reasons. A former Collector of Internal Revenue, under whom he served
and by whom he wvas separated from the service, makes the following
statement regarding him in a letter dated May 9, 1913:
Mr. Vanderford was an officer in the service when I was appointed
Collector in 1898 and had been for four years prior to my appoint-
ment. He served under me for practically a year. I regarded him
as one of the best officers in the service and after ten years' experience
as Collector I think I can truthfully say he w~as as good an officer as I
ever knew. I separated him from the service in order to appoint a man
of my own party.

states that he has personally known Mr. Vanderford for many years, that
he is a man of sterling integrity, honest and fearless, and in his opinion
possesses just such traits of character as would make a competent and
efficient revenue officer. The records of the Internal Revenue Bureau
show that he rendered satisfactory service and was an efficient employe.

mendation of the Secretary of the Treasury and the Commi

head:

To prohibit the unauthorized use of flying machines.
By' virtue of the authority vested in me, I hereby establish the following
order for the Canal Zone:
Section I. It shall be unlawful for any person to operate an aeroplane,
balloon or living machine of any kind in or across the Canal Zone without
the written authority of the Chief Executive of the Canal Zone.
Section 2 It shall be unlawful for any, person to take or make a
photograph, picture or sketch of any kind of the fortifications or other
military works in the Canal Zone from any aeroplane, balloon or flying
machine of any kind without the written consent of the Chief Executive
of the Canal Zone.
Section 3. A violation of any of the provisions of this order shall be
punishable by a fine not exceeding One Thousand dollars or by imprison-
ment in jail not exceeding one year, or by both such fine and imprisonment
in the discretion of the Court.

its publication in the Canal Record.

on September Ia, [898, notice of his removal alleging "inefficiency". No

Mr. William B. Green may be reinstated as a compositor in the
Weather Bureau without reference to the time limit imposed by the civil
service rules.
Mr. Green's services as a compositor were terminated on December
31, 1910, after more than twenty years' service. The reason given at the
time was that a reduction of the force was necessary because of the trans-
fer of certain work from the Weather Bureau to the Government Printing
Office. The Secretary of Agriculture with the concurrence of the Civil
Service Commission recommends the reinstatement because there is reason
to believe that Mr. Green was unfairly dealt with because of certain testi-
mony he had given in a case which resulted in the reprimand of the Chief
of the Weather Bureau.

head:

To punish deported persons who return to the Canal Zone.
By virtue of the authority vested in me I hereby establish the follow-
ing Order for the Canal Zone :
Section I. Any person who, after having served a sentence of im-
prisonment in the Canal Zone and after being deported therefrom, returns
to the Canal Zone shall be deemed guilty of felony and punished by
imprisonment in the penitentiary for a term of not less than six months
nor more than twvo years, and upon the completion of his sentence he
shall be removed from the Canal Zone in accordance with the laws and
orders relating to deportation. An entry into the Canal Zone, for any
purpose, shall be sufficient to constitute a return to the Zone within the
meaning of this Order; provided, however, that in a case of necessity the
Chief Executive of the Canal Zone, in his discretion, may grant a permit
to any such person to return to the Canal Zone temporarily, but should
he remain in the Canal Zone after the time specified in the permit he shall
be deemed guilty of a violation of this Order and punished as therein
provided.
Section 2 The Executive Order of May 2, 1911, providing a punish-
ment for deported persons who return to the Canal Zone is hereby
repealed.
Section 3. This Order shall take effect thirty days from and after its
publication in the Canal Record.
WOODROW WILSON

25 SeftI., 1913.

head:
Executive ether.
Amendment of the Civil Service Rules.
Schedule A, Subdivision XII, relating to the Interstate Commerce
Commission, is hereby amended as follows:
i. The word "three" in the first paragraph is stricken out and the
word "five" substituted therefor.
2. New paragraphs are added as follows:
3. One director under said act.
4. One supervisor of land appraisals under said act.
5. One chief accountant under said act.
As amended the Subdivision will read as follows:
X II. Interstate Commerce Commission.
i. Five experts to be members of an advisory board under the act
of March i, 1913, providing for the valuation of the prop-
erty of carriers.
2Five members of a board of engineers under said act.
3. One director under said act.
4. One supervisor of land appraisals under said act.
5. One chief accountant under said act.
The Interstate Commerce Commission, with the concurrence of the
Civil Service Commission, recommends the exception of these additional
supervisory and advisory positions because of the peculiar and unusual
qualifications required.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
29 October, 1913.
[No. 1851-1
